title: Local Meeting Export
user: macOS knowledge workers who need a background, local-only meeting recorder whose transcript and notes land predictably in their own Markdown vault.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Asks for a macOS background daemon using local transcription, diarization and speaker identification after Granola restricted export into Obsidian.
Meetily user reports Whisper mangling client names and domain jargon and asks for local vocabulary hints; accuracy and ownership of output remain unresolved.

recurrence: Two independent 2026 local-meeting workflows; the direct request lists background capture, local processing and Markdown export as non-negotiable.
current_workaround: Use cloud recorders, manually copy notes, or maintain a brittle third-party export plugin.
incumbents_and_gap: Granola, Otter and Fireflies are cloud-centric; Meetily and Lumi cover capture, but a reliable local daemon-to-vault export contract with glossary correction is still fragmented.
smallest_useful_product: Signed macOS menu-bar app: capture selected system/mic devices, invoke a user-installed local Whisper-compatible engine, apply a per-vault glossary, and atomically write Markdown plus audio link. Non-goals: bot joining, cloud transcription, team workspace or AI meeting advice.
success_measure: In a 20-meeting pilot, 90% of recordings produce a Markdown note in the selected vault without manual copying and named-entity corrections fall below two per meeting.
monetization: one-time — privacy-sensitive individuals can pay for a dependable native utility without an ongoing recording-data subscription.
constraints: Explicit recording consent indicators; macOS Screen Recording/Microphone permissions; all audio and model execution local by default; never bypass meeting-platform rules.
why_distinct: It is an owned-file export and vocabulary-correction layer, not another meeting bot or generic transcription SaaS.

title: VRAM Burn-in Kit
user: PC builders and local-AI operators who need a repeatable, bootable-or-desktop test that finds intermittent GPU VRAM faults before trusting a card with long jobs.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Explicitly asks for a MemTest86+-like VRAM tester for GPUs.
A user documents reproducible RTX 5080 stalls across unrelated renderers without a crash or Xid error, illustrating why ordinary crash logs do not establish GPU-memory health.

recurrence: A direct tester request and a separate reproducible silent-stall report in 2026; faulty/unstable VRAM can corrupt expensive rendering and inference runs without a clear driver crash.
current_workaround: Run a game benchmark, stress a model, inspect vendor telemetry, or replace hardware based on suspicion.
incumbents_and_gap: MemTest86 targets system RAM; OCCT and vendor diagnostics are broad stress suites. The gap is an auditable VRAM-pattern test with a small result bundle that distinguishes allocation, transfer and compute-path failures.
smallest_useful_product: Signed Windows/Linux desktop utility that selects a GPU, runs bounded fill/copy/readback and shader-pattern passes, temperature-aware retries, and exports a signed JSON/HTML casefile. Non-goals: overclocking, repair, mining or driver tuning.
success_measure: On seeded CUDA/Vulkan fault simulations, the tool identifies the failing test stage in 95% of runs and users can attach a one-file report to a support request.
monetization: one-time — episodic hardware diagnosis is a clear local-tool purchase, with a free basic pass for trust.
constraints: Warn before sustained load; cap power/temperature where APIs permit; use vendor-supported APIs only; report confidence rather than claiming to certify hardware.
why_distinct: It produces a memory-specific diagnostic receipt rather than being another benchmark chart or GPU tuner.

title: APK Provenance Locker
user: Android sideloaders who need to keep a verifiable inventory of their own APKs, signing certificates, install source and rollback-safe backups as platform rules tighten.

evidence.quote_or_summary: An Android user asks how to prepare for impending sideloading changes while depending on both F-Droid and Play Store apps.
Feature request for EU SideStore PAL specifically cites avoiding the app-slot cost of current sideloading, showing continuing installation-friction demand.

recurrence: Two independent sideloading threads in 2025; restriction risk is severe because an app or an older compatible version can become hard to reinstall.
current_workaround: Scatter APK files across Downloads, trust a store history, or rerun a sideload tool without knowing the original signer or version.
incumbents_and_gap: F-Droid, Obtainium, AltStore and SideStore install apps; none is primarily a user-owned, cross-source evidence locker that detects signer drift and prepares an offline restoration set.
smallest_useful_product: Android APK plus companion desktop app that inventories user-selected APKs, verifies v1/v2/v3 signer lineage, records source URL and hash, encrypts an exportable manifest, and warns before an incompatible downgrade. Non-goals: app-store bypass, cracked apps, account provisioning or piracy discovery.
success_measure: A pilot user can export and later validate a 20-app restoration manifest with zero hash/signature mismatches and identify every unexpected signer change.
monetization: one-time — it protects a personal software collection locally and should not require a cloud account.
constraints: Never distribute copyrighted APKs or evade platform controls; request only storage/install permissions needed; encrypted backups remain device/user controlled.
why_distinct: It is provenance and recoverability tooling around lawful user-held APKs, not an alternative app store.

title: EPUB Annotation Bridge
user: Readers who sideload legal EPUBs and need highlights and notes to survive moving between Calibre-managed libraries and e-readers.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Reader wants an open e-reader with Calibre-compatible EPUB sideloading and annotation support, explicitly rejecting lock-in.

A KOReader user reports a device-specific refresh/reboot defect after testing without plugins, a reminder that e-reader behavior is device-dependent and local library data needs portable escape hatches.

recurrence: The 2025 request combines sideloading, Calibre and annotations; device-specific reader failures make exportable reading data more valuable.
current_workaround: Keep notes trapped in a device database, export clippings manually, or avoid annotations when changing devices.
incumbents_and_gap: Calibre manages files and KOReader/Kindle/Kobo each store annotations differently. Existing plugins are device-specific; there is no small desktop round-trip tool centered on a stable, readable annotation ledger.
smallest_useful_product: Desktop app that watches a Calibre library plus mounted reader, imports supported highlight stores into a book-CFI ledger, exports Markdown/JSON, and writes only safe sidecar files. Non-goals: DRM removal, ebook sales, reader firmware or cloud sync service.
success_measure: For supported EPUBs, 95% of imported highlights retain the correct chapter and quote after an export/import round trip across two reader families.
monetization: one-time — personal-library portability has durable value and a local purchase aligns with the no-lock-in need.
constraints: No DRM circumvention; support only documented/exportable reader data; preserve original files; handle copyrighted books entirely on device.
why_distinct: The durable artifact is a reader-independent annotation ledger, not a new ebook reader or Calibre replacement.

title: Diagram Source Studio
user: Engineers who keep D2 or Mermaid diagrams in Git and need a fast native editor that catches broken render output before a diagram is committed.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Asks what a native desktop diagrams-as-code editor should provide, citing cumbersome web editors and needs such as autocomplete, editable PNG/SVG and offline docs.
A user reports that Mermaid renderers omit arcs in a subgraph, demonstrating the need to review actual rendered output rather than source text alone.

recurrence: A direct native-editor request plus a separate rendering correctness failure in 2025; broken diagrams silently degrade documentation and architecture review.
current_workaround: Use browser editors, a general code editor preview, or discover renderer differences in CI/README after committing.
incumbents_and_gap: Mermaid Live Editor, D2 Playground and VS Code extensions are useful but web/IDE dependent. The gap is an offline, file-native workbench that compares renderer versions and preserves editable source in exported artifacts.
smallest_useful_product: Tauri desktop app with split source/canvas, offline syntax reference, diagnostics, renderer-version matrix preview, and SVG/PNG export embedding source metadata. Non-goals: whiteboard collaboration, diagram hosting, AI diagram generation or replacing Git.
success_measure: In a pilot repository, 90% of intentionally seeded rendering differences are surfaced before export and an editable source round trip preserves byte-for-byte source.
monetization: one-time — a focused local authoring tool fits developer purchase behavior; the core file format remains open.
constraints: Sandbox renderers and untrusted SVG; never execute embedded links/scripts; preserve file encoding and source control friendliness.
why_distinct: It is a rendering-verification workbench for source-controlled diagrams, not another canvas or AI image generator.

title: Presence Bridge
user: Two-to-ten person businesses that need a clean desktop chat presence indicator and one-click contact handoff without moving their conversations into another full chat suite.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A business pair seeking a desktop chat app says online presence is essential and reports trying Telegram, Signal, Element, Rocket.Chat, Discord and Teams without a satisfactory fit.
The 2025 Lobsters discussion on Delta Chat reflects continuing interest in alternative cross-platform desktop messaging rather than a single dominant business-chat client.

recurrence: The HN asker exhausts six established products over presence and clutter; the separate 2025 messaging discussion shows continued appetite for smaller cross-platform alternatives.
current_workaround: Keep multiple chat clients open, ask by text whether someone is available, or accept ad/upsell-heavy suites.
incumbents_and_gap: Signal, Telegram, Element, Teams and Discord are full messaging products. The narrow gap is a privacy-respecting presence and contact-launch layer that does not try to replace a chosen transport.
smallest_useful_product: Cross-platform tray app with manually set and calendar-derived availability, a local team roster, and configurable deep links to the team's existing chat/call tools. Non-goals: message transport, contact scraping, employee surveillance or a new social network.
success_measure: A five-person pilot resolves 80% of availability checks by seeing the tray roster before sending a message, while no message content leaves existing clients.
monetization: freemium — free local roster for small groups; a paid encrypted roster relay can fund optional multi-device sync.
constraints: Presence must be opt-in and transparent; no background keystroke/activity inference; use documented deep-link APIs only.
why_distinct: It adds the missing availability layer around existing communication choices instead of cloning a chat application.

title: iOS Review Gate
user: Small iOS teams that need a local, reviewable release packet and realistic queue plan before submitting builds to App Review.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A small team asks how others handle two-week iOS submissions when review times and rejections create a queue of blocked builds.
Fastlane users report intermittent App Store upload/version handling failure, showing that even established automation leaves release-state ambiguity.

recurrence: A direct 2026 planning question and a separate 2025 upload-state failure; release uncertainty is a schedule blocker for small teams without dedicated release management.
current_workaround: Maintain a spreadsheet, inspect App Store Connect manually, and find missing metadata or wrong build numbers late in the submission.
incumbents_and_gap: Fastlane and Xcode automate builds/uploads; App Store Connect owns submission. Neither makes a repository-local, human-reviewable packet that says exactly what artifact, metadata and known-review risk is being queued.
smallest_useful_product: CLI that reads an IPA/archive metadata export and release YAML, checks version/build consistency, screenshot/localization completeness, privacy-manifest declarations and produces a dated Markdown submission packet. Non-goals: submitting on a user's behalf, bypassing Apple review, analytics or release hosting.
success_measure: Before submission, pilots catch 90% of seeded metadata/version inconsistencies and generate a complete release packet in under five minutes.
monetization: one-time — an episodic release-control tool should run locally and remain usable between launches.
constraints: Do not scrape private App Store Connect data; use local exports or official APIs with least-privilege tokens; Apple policy changes require versioned rules.
why_distinct: It is a release decision record and preflight gate, not another build-upload service.

title: Installer Release Doctor
user: CLI authors who need to ship a signed, installable release across package channels without becoming experts in every distribution system.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A CLI author gives up on PPA publishing after isolated builds, per-Ubuntu toolchains, packaging complexity and opaque logs consume more time than the tool itself.
A 244-reaction request asks for a standalone Windows installer because Store-based installation is unavailable under corporate, offline and personal constraints.

recurrence: Independent Linux and Windows install-channel pain in 2026; packaging is severe enough to stop publication and exclude locked-down users.
current_workaround: Hand-write packaging per platform, ship an archive with curl instructions, or abandon a channel after CI failures.
incumbents_and_gap: GoReleaser, cargo-dist, nfpm and package-specific CI handle portions. The missing small layer is a release-readiness diagnosis that verifies an already-built artifact against channel constraints and explains the next repair.
smallest_useful_product: CLI reads release artifacts and a declarative channel manifest, runs local checks for archive layout, signatures, SBOM/provenance, package metadata and installer upgrade paths, then emits GitHub Actions annotations and a channel matrix. Non-goals: credential storage, package hosting, code signing service or a new package manager.
success_measure: For fixture releases with seeded defects, it identifies 95% of channel-blocking issues before CI upload and reduces first successful multi-channel release time by 30%.
monetization: freemium — an open local checker earns ecosystem trust; paid policy packs/support serve companies with compliance requirements.
constraints: Never handle signing keys beyond invoking an existing local signer; validate untrusted archives safely; keep platform policies versioned and explain uncertainty.
why_distinct: It checks and explains installer release readiness rather than trying to replace every package builder or registry.

title: Worktree Agent Pulse
user: Solo developers and tiny teams running several CLI coding agents in Git worktrees who need a native overview of activity, blocked prompts and branch safety without switching terminal tabs.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A monorepo developer running three to six CLI agents says terminal-tab management is the bottleneck and existing options either replace the CLI or do not understand worktrees.
A 480-reaction request asks an agent CLI for Agent Client Protocol stdio/JSON-RPC mode, confirming strong demand for interoperable control and status surfaces around agent command-line tools.

recurrence: The direct 2026 ask is specific to parallel worktrees; a separate high-reaction 2026 request for interoperable agent-CLI control shows the same ecosystem is rapidly operationalizing multiple tools.
current_workaround: Name terminals manually, poll tabs, run tmux scripts, or use an agent-specific paid dashboard.
incumbents_and_gap: tmux, Zellij, Warp, Ghostty and Conductor manage terminals or agent workflows. The gap is a read-only worktree-centric pulse board that coexists with the user's chosen terminal and agent CLI.
smallest_useful_product: Cross-platform tray/desktop app that discovers Git worktrees, tails opt-in agent status adapters, shows dirty/ahead/blocked state, and opens the exact terminal/worktree. Non-goals: issuing model prompts, controlling agent permissions, replacing Git or recording terminal contents by default.
success_measure: A five-worktree pilot finds a blocked agent or uncommitted branch from the board in under 10 seconds in 90% of prompted trials.
monetization: one-time — a local developer cockpit has individual utility and should work offline.
constraints: Opt-in adapters only; avoid capture of prompt/output content; protect repository paths; use Git read operations unless user triggers an action.
why_distinct: It observes heterogeneous existing CLIs through worktree state instead of becoming another agent or terminal emulator.

title: Local Model Residency
user: Privacy-conscious desktop users who run local models but need a plain explanation of model memory residency, unload/reload churn and which local client is consuming GPU/RAM.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Asks why ready-to-use offline desktop LLMs remain hard for ordinary users despite privacy and connectivity advantages.
Feature request says DBeaver Community lacks local-Ollama integration, showing sustained demand to keep AI-assisted workflows local instead of tied to a hosted tier.

recurrence: The 2026 audience request is for a ready working local experience; a separate local-runtime request shows technically capable users also prioritize local operation over hosted-only features.
current_workaround: Watch Activity Monitor/nvidia-smi, guess at keep-alive settings, or restart clients when a model becomes slow.
incumbents_and_gap: Ollama, LM Studio and Jan run models; system monitors show processes. The gap is a small vendor-neutral tray utility that translates runtime/model ownership and churn into actionable local diagnostics.
smallest_useful_product: Menu-bar/tray app that reads supported local-runtime status endpoints and OS process metrics, shows model load owner, GPU/RAM footprint, reload events and a safe copyable diagnostic bundle. Non-goals: model download, prompt logging, model serving, chat UI or cloud inference.
success_measure: In reproduced two-client tests, it attributes 90% of load/unload events to a process/runtime and users identify the reload source without opening a terminal.
monetization: free — broad runtime support and trust matter more than monetizing a diagnostic; paid enterprise adapters can follow.
constraints: No prompt/completion collection; query only documented local endpoints; disclose incomplete attribution; keep diagnostics local unless explicitly exported.
why_distinct: It makes local-model resource behavior understandable without becoming another model launcher or chat client.

title: Manuscript Entity Indexer
user: Novelists writing multilingual manuscripts who need a local, lightweight character/place/alias ledger and continuity search without uploading drafts or shipping a giant model.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A local-first writing-app developer asks for CJK/Latin entity extraction of characters, aliases, relationships and timeline facts without bundling a huge model.
The repeated local-model unload/reload report reinforces the requester's concern that making a large local model a dependency harms normal-desktop usability.

recurrence: A detailed 2026 multilingual story-memory need plus concrete local-model resource churn; privacy, repeated indexing speed and CJK name handling make this more than generic note taking.
current_workaround: Maintain a manual story bible, search chapters by hand, use cloud writing assistants, or attach a large local model to every edit.
incumbents_and_gap: Scrivener, Obsidian and Sudowrite organize manuscripts; generic NER libraries assume English or cloud models. The gap is an offline, explainable index with CJK-aware alias proposals and no generative rewriting.
smallest_useful_product: Desktop app that indexes a chosen Markdown/DOCX folder, extracts candidate entities with dictionaries and lightweight rules, lets the author merge/rename aliases, and offers a chapter-linked timeline/ledger. Non-goals: text generation, training on manuscripts, cloud collaboration or literary judgment.
success_measure: On author-reviewed multilingual sample manuscripts, 80% of accepted recurring person/place mentions are found with fewer than 10% false alias merges.
monetization: one-time — authors can own an offline drafting companion and avoid recurring AI usage fees.
constraints: Offline by default; no manuscript telemetry; preserve source files; clearly label heuristic suggestions and support Unicode/CJK normalization safely.
why_distinct: It is an author-controlled continuity index, not a thin generative-writing wrapper.

title: Agent CLI Contract
user: CLI maintainers whose commands will be driven by coding agents and scripts, and who need to verify stable machine contracts without making the human CLI unpleasant.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Asks practitioners which command-line design choices matter when AI agents are the users of a tool.
A 565-reaction Codex CLI feature request seeks auto-detected/installed language servers, demonstrating that agent-oriented CLI capabilities and machine-readable diagnostics are active demand.

recurrence: A direct 2026 design question and a high-reaction agent-CLI capability request; unstable output and unclear failure modes make agents brittle and users distrust automation.
current_workaround: Hand-test prompts, parse colored terminal output, or build custom smoke tests for each command.
incumbents_and_gap: clap/cobra/argparse generate CLIs; shell tests verify examples. The missing tool is a local contract runner that tests exit codes, structured output, idempotency and error recoverability from an agent's point of view.
smallest_useful_product: CLI that runs a declarative fixture suite against another CLI, snapshots TTY and JSON modes, validates error taxonomy, detects nondeterministic fields, and writes a Markdown/JSON contract report. Non-goals: an agent framework, natural-language command generation, terminal emulator or benchmark league table.
success_measure: For seeded CLIs, it detects 90% of output/exit-code contract regressions and a maintainer can add a first contract suite in under 15 minutes.
monetization: free — an open cross-language contract format maximizes adoption; paid support/adapters are possible later.
constraints: Fixtures must run in isolated temp directories; never execute arbitrary generated commands; redact environment secrets and make network use opt-in.
why_distinct: It tests deterministic interfaces for agents and humans, rather than wrapping a CLI in another LLM layer.
